newsitem.title: USA: Johnstown America Q2 car shipments up.
newsitem.headline: Johnstown America Q2 car shipments up.

text.p: Johnstown America Industries Inc said Thursday it shipped 1,043 new and rebuilt cars in the second quarter, compared with 760 in the year-ago quarter and 532 cars in the first quarter.
Order backlog stood at 1,949 cars as of June 30, compared to 774 at year-end 1996.

"Although demand for new freight cars remains at low levels, the increase in our shipments and backlog suggests that the market decline may have bottomed out," Thomas Begel, chairman, said in a statement.
Earlier, Johnstown America reported a second quarter net loss of $0.05 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.13. Revenues rose to $158.2 million from $133.3 million.

"In the last several quarters, our truck components and iron castings operations have continued to produce strong results, while our freight car operations continued to struggle with low production volumes," Begel said.
Truck components sales were $75.1 million in the quarter, up from $60.5 million a year ago. Iron castings sales were $34.1 million, up from $30.8 million.
Freight car revenues increased to $49.1 million from $41.9 million last year.
